_about: THE BOATS (Track BB, 2026-10-10): the patrol boat and the supply boat, as the generators in scripts/render/boat_art.gd draw them. EVERY VALUE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track BB; none is a decision. What is Alex's (decision water-layer, 2026-10-10): at least one small boat, two proposed by the lead ('Sounds good'): an armed patrol boat and an unarmed supply boat; they are part of the environment with real patrols but no specific part in the mission ('Correct, part of the environment with real patrols but no specific part in the mission'), so they are real units that sail a route and can be hit, and the patrol boat's guns stay quiet. How they LOOK is a board (variants/boats/): board.json there has chosen: null. Record shape as in data/terrain/terrain.json: {value, _proposed, _reason}; keys starting with _ are documentation. LENGTHS ARE METRES; angles are radians in the code, fractions are fractions of the hull's length or beam. Colours are ROLES (base, shade, toward, alpha) resolved by scripts/render/ink_roles.gd against the palette: no hex anywhere (working rule 6). A look is a set of RANGES the generator draws from with the sheet's own seed rule (unitSeed on the scene seed, the unit index and the look's variant), so a look is the same boat on every machine.

rule._reason: PROPOSED working default, nothing is chosen. plane: a boat is drawn at the planes' marker scale -- the same pixels per metre as a plane at every zoom (data/ui/ui.json marker.true_scale: plane_px 36 for the 9 m light fighter at zoom 1 over the map's 2 px/m is a multiplier of 2, so 4 px per metre at zoom 1; at the planning zoom 0.35 the light fighter's 14 px floor (plane_min_px) makes it 14/9 = 1.56 px per metre), so a boat keeps its TRUE ratio to a plane (a 27 m patrol boat is three light fighters long) and reads next to one at every zoom, which is what the design doc asks of ships ('drawn at a scale that reads next to the planes'). Boats are real units now (Alex), so the marker layer's rule is the one they follow. map: a boat is drawn at the MAP's scale like a house or a bridge (2 px per metre x zoom: 2 at zoom 1, 0.7 at the planning zoom), which fits rivers, bridges and houses but makes a patrol boat 19 px long at the planning zoom. The board shows both on its scale strip; a boat on a RIVER only fits a 40 to 80 m river under 'map' (36 m at 4 px/m is 144 px, the river 80 to 160).

sun._about: The map's own light is read from data/params/render_defaults.json (sun_direction 315, sun_elevation 46, shadow_strength 0.44); nothing here repeats it.

patrol._about: A small armed coastal patrol boat: a sharp or blunt hull, a gun mount fore and aft, a small bridge house with a funnel and a mast. Its guns are light anti-aircraft guns and STAY QUIET in the strike (Alex: no part in the mission), so they are drawn trained fore and aft, stowed, with no fire.

unit_index._reason: the unit sheet's UNITS list ends at 6 (the radio tower); the next free index feeds unitSeed, as the other units' do

size_m._reason: a WWII motor gunboat / harbour defence launch is 20 to 35 m; 27 is three light fighters (9 m) long and a bit more than a bomber's span (20 m)

beam_m._reason: beam about a fifth of the length, as a gunboat's

freeboard_m._reason: the hull's side above the water; its shadow on the sea is this long away from the sun (x the sun's length 0.97)

gunwale_m._reason: the strip of side deck outside the deck line

wake_len_m._reason: the wake reaches this far aft of the stern at patrol speed (about 2.3 hulls)

p1.title: Cutter
p1.about: A sharp, long-bowed hull with a transom, twin gun mounts under shields fore and aft, a bridge house, funnel, mast, a dinghy and depth charges. Everything is drawn.

p2.title: Picket boat
p2.about: A short, beamy hull with a round stern and a bluff bow, single guns in round tubs, a taller bridge house. Fewer parts: no depth charges, no dinghy, no rafts.

p3.title: Bare minimum
p3.about: The same hull as the cutter drawn with the least that still reads: the hull, two gun marks and a house. No planking, no deck line, no funnel, no mast, no small gear. Reads best at the planning zoom.

p4.title: Whaleback gunboat
p4.about: A long, slender hull with a turtle-backed foredeck (a broken deck line), one big twin mount forward and a single gun aft, a low house far aft. The gun forward is the picture.

supply._about: An unarmed supply boat on a route: a small coaster or a barge with hatches and deck cargo.

unit_index._reason: the next unit index after the patrol boat's

size_m._reason: a small coaster or a canal barge is 25 to 45 m; 34 is a little over a bomber's span times one and a half

beam_m._reason: beam about a fifth to a quarter of the length: a cargo boat is beamier than a gunboat

freeboard_m._reason: a light coaster's side above the water

gunwale_m._reason: the strip of side deck outside the deck line

wake_len_m._reason: slower than the patrol boat: a shorter wake

s1.title: Coaster
s1.about: A pointed bow, two hatches under tarpaulins forward, a house with a funnel and a bridge aft, a derrick on the foredeck. The accent panel is painted on the forward hatch's tarpaulin.

s2.title: Barge with deck cargo
s2.about: A flat-bottomed scow: a blunt bow and stern, a tiny cabin aft, no hatches, and a load of crates, barrels and a tarpaulined stack lashed on deck. The accent panel is on the cabin roof.

s3.title: Lighter
s3.about: A long, narrow hull with ONE long hold under a battened tarpaulin from forward to aft and a wheelhouse at the stern. The least drawn of the cargo boats.

s4.title: Coaster, deck-loaded
s4.about: The coaster with one hatch and the rest of the deck stacked with barrel clusters and crates. The house and funnel are amidships-aft. Everything is drawn.

wakes._about: Three treatments of the wake behind a boat under way (variants/boats/). The same boat in each. A boat at anchor has none. Lines are ink at alpha steps, dots are the paper ramp's object fill and ink, the wash is the object fill at a low alpha: no new hue.

spread_deg._reason: the half angle of the V the wake opens at (a ship's Kelvin wedge is 19.5 degrees; a tighter V reads as faster in a small drawing and keeps two boats' wakes apart)

ink_v.title: Ink V
ink_v.about: Two lines from the bow along the hull and out in a V, an inner pair from midships, a broken line down the stern wash, small crest ticks across the V.

foam.title: Foam stipple
foam.about: Dots in the V: dense paper-cream foam hugging the two edges and the stern wash, thinning with distance, a few ink dots for grain, a spray of dots at the bow.

wash.title: Pale wash trail
wash.about: A tapering trail of the paper tone behind the stern, ragged-edged, laid in six thin washes that fade out, a pale sliver along each side of the bow, and a broken ink line on each outer edge.

roles._about: Every colour the boats draw, as a role (base, shade, toward, t, alpha). Hue is reserved for paper, ink, shadow and the side accents; lightness is the ramp off paper; material is linework. The only role that is not on that rule is the PLACEHOLDER water (below).
roles._water_placeholder: PLACEHOLDER, NOT A PICK: the water's look is Track WB's board (variants/water/). Here it is the one shadow tint mixed 42 percent toward paper, so the boats and wakes can be judged on a blue wash; it is not a role the game uses.
